## Pitch

OpenShouter is a FOSS Android announcer that reads notifications aloud, loops incoming caller ID until the ring stops, and speaks battery, power, and location-aware events. It combines Voice Notify-style notification TTS with classic Shouter hardware and telephony features, using only open Android APIs — no Google Play Services, Firebase, or tracking.

## Features

- Notification reader with custom TTS format strings, per-app filters, and regex ignore/replace rules
- Looping caller ID announcements that stop on answer, reject, or missed call
- Battery, charger, shake-to-silence, flip-to-mute, and screen on/off mute controls
- Quiet hours, headset/Bluetooth-only mode, and FOSS geofence rules (no Play Services)
- Foreground service, Quick Settings tile, and home-screen master on/off widget
- Local-only history via Room; MIT licensed and F-Droid-friendly

## Quick start

1. Read `docs/START_HERE.md`, `docs/CURSOR_MODES.md`, and `BUILD_PLAN.md` Sequential lane.
2. Install Android Studio (or SDK 34+) with JDK 17; open `examples/android/`.
3. Follow Sprint 1 in `BUILD_PLAN.md` to scaffold the app modules (do not copy proprietary SDKs).
4. On a device or emulator, enable Notification Listener and required runtime permissions (`[ADB]`).

## Install

Requires JDK 17 and Android SDK (compile/target 35, min 26). Clone the repo, open `examples/android/`, and run `./gradlew assembleDebug` (or `gradlew.bat` on Windows). Sideload the debug APK or wait for GitHub Releases / F-Droid once Sprint 1+ ships. No Play Store In-App Updates.
